identityTradability.exchangeName: Meta Platforms, Inc. - Class A Common Stock

source-integrity.name: provenance and freshness
source-integrity.basis: Primary operating evidence is current through Q2 2026 and market evidence through 2026-09-24; duplicate origins are collapsed rather than counted as independent corroboration.

structural-causal.name: AI infrastructure causal conversion
structural-causal.basis: Revenue, ad impressions and ad pricing grew strongly while capex accelerated sharply; the bridge from infrastructure spend to durable incremental monetization remains the key falsifiable link.

structural-causal.name: scenario robustness
structural-causal.basis: Large cash generation and scaled ad demand support resilience, while unusually high infrastructure intensity creates a successor bottleneck in power, compute deployment and return-on-capital conversion.

discovery-weak-signals.name: core monetization scale
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Both ad volume and pricing grew double digits while revenue rose 28%.

adversarial-red-team.name: capital intensity and conversion risk
adversarial-red-team.basis: Rapid infrastructure spending materially compresses near-term free-cash conversion even as core advertising execution remains strong.

expectations-execution.name: AI investment conversion
expectations-execution.basis: Strong revenue/advertising execution is paired with unusually high capital intensity, so future returns on infrastructure are a key expectation test.

thesisQuality.basis: 28% revenue growth with simultaneous double-digit ad-impression and ad-price growth demonstrates exceptional current product-market fit; durability is capped by AI-capex conversion uncertainty.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Revenue growth is strong and liquidity substantial, but operating margin compressed to 31% and Q2 free cash flow was $784M amid $31.08B capex.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: At the 2026-09-24 close of $777.59 after a sharp rally, valuation requires continued strong growth and AI conversion rather than offering clear deep-value asymmetry.

catalystScore.basis: AI product momentum and the next earnings read-through provide identifiable monetization tests, while economics remain partly early.

governancePower.basis: SEC reporting and operating execution are established, but no fresh proxy package supports a stronger band.

alignment2036.basis: Scaled digital communications, AI systems and advertising infrastructure are durable technology capabilities with broad economic relevance.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Apps, messaging and AI products reuse compute/model infrastructure across products, while advertising remains the dominant economic engine.

bottleneckControl.basis: Meta controls massive user distribution, data and model deployment, but underlying compute and power supply remain externally dependent.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Large cash generation and global app usage support resilience while fixed AI infrastructure commitments increase downside sensitivity.

substitutionResilience.basis: Scale, network effects and advertiser tooling create replacement friction, but user attention and AI interfaces remain competitive.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Financial capacity supports procurement, but the AI build depends on external semiconductor, power and data-center supply chains.

pricingPower.basis: Average price per ad rose 12% while ad impressions rose 14%, directly demonstrating strong current monetization and pricing capture.

riskEvidence.basis: High AI infrastructure intensity, margin compression and legal/regulatory exposure are material, offset by strong demand and liquidity.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Operating claims have issuer and SEC support and current market evidence; confidence is reduced by missing fresh proxy detail and undisclosed project-level AI returns.

scoreRecord.thesis: Meta combines exceptional advertising monetization scale with AI-driven product optionality, but the investment case depends materially on converting a very large infrastructure cycle into durable incremental monetization.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: AI/data-center capex grows faster than durable monetization and compresses free-cash-flow conversion and returns on capital.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Q3 2026 operating results and evidence that AI-product adoption converts into measurable monetization or efficiency gains.

items.risk: Q2 costs and expenses rose 55% year over year and capex was $31.08B, making AI infrastructure intensity a material execution burden.
Legal charges, severance and rapid infrastructure spending can obscure normalized cost conversion and raise disappointment risk if AI monetization lags.
If incremental AI infrastructure fails to sustain engagement, ad efficiency or new monetization at adequate returns, the current positive causal chain weakens despite strong top-line growth.
High fixed infrastructure commitments raise downside sensitivity if AI monetization or engagement benefits arrive slower than spending growth.

contradictions.claimB: Near-term free-cash conversion is weak because infrastructure spending is exceptionally high.
contradictions.resolution: These are simultaneous operating facts rather than mutually exclusive claims; the unresolved economic question is future return on the investment, treated as a non-gating unknown rather than a fabricated contradiction.

unknowns.unknown: Scout does not infer return on incremental AI capex from one quarter of operating data.
No canonical valuation or entry-price conclusion is asserted by Scout.
Incremental return on the newest AI/data-center capex is not separable from current quarter disclosures.
Current evidence does not quantify the portion of AI capex that is maintenance versus growth or its eventual project-level return.
